title: Migration sprint - limited availability & empowerment notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratch for the upcoming infra migration sprint (weekend window). This is a lightweight comms + agent empowerment crib I want to share with oncall, support L2, and the product ops leads. Not final — planning to pull these bullets into a tidy all-hands note if we lock timeline.

Background (short):
- We are migrating a subset of the inference control plane to the new dataplane routing layer (thin-safe rollout). This reduces cross-region latency and enables smarter routing by weight.
- Risk: transient API 503s for small percentage (target <2%) of requests during the cutover if session affinity moves between backends.
- Reason for weekend window: lower traffic and easier capacity buffer.

High-level goals for comms:
- Be transparent about limited availability window and who is impacted.
- Give concise action items and scripts so support can respond quickly without escalating every ticket.
- Surface automatic fallbacks/end-user experience so product teams can adjust expectations.
- Provide a clear escalation path and a quick rollback play (if needed).

Planned window (tentative):
- Saturday 2026-03-21 02:00 - 06:00 PT (4h primary window)
- Pre-check and smoke-run Friday 2026-03-20 22:00 - 23:30 PT
- Post-validation and follow-up Monday 2026-03-23 09:00 - 11:00 PT

Impacted surfaces (short):
- Redwood API (hosted inference) — small fraction of requests may receive 503/504 or increased tail latency during cutover.
- Streaming sessions may see reconnects; clients using function/tool-calling could experience duplicated events if retry logic is naive.
- Dedicated and Private customers are not in scope for this migration.

Internal audience mapping:
- Primary: oncall (SRE), support L2, product leads for hosted-api routes
- Secondary: Sales/CS (heads-up), Trust & Safety (monitoring for abuse signals), Docs (update status page if needed)

Support empowerment checklist (what to give L2 so they can act without escalating):
1) Diagnosis quick check:
   - Ask for: request timestamp, model/route, region header, API key suffix, client IP/time offset, and logs link.
   - Quick indicators: multiple 503s across different keys in same minute -> likely migration-related; single-user repeated 503s -> investigate config/ratelimit.
2) Standard reply template (short):
   - "Thanks — we're running a planned infrastructure migration during [WINDOW]. You may see transient errors; if you can share the request id and timestamp we'll trace. If the issue persists beyond 10 minutes, we'll escalate."
3) When to escalate to SRE oncall:
   - Error rate > 5% sustained for 10m on a single region or route.
   - High-severity customer complaining of production outage (SLA contract).
   - Automated alert: INF-MIGRATION-CRIT generated by canary check.
4) Quick mitigation steps L2 can try (non-destructive):
   - Suggest clients retry with exponential backoff and idempotency keys (if using streaming, advise reconnect rather than client-side concurrent retries).
   - Advise to switch to a compatible model variant (if customer is using a large quantized variant known to be routed to new pool) — point them to internal model fallback table.

Support reply examples (short, multiple channels):
- Slack quick reply snippet (public channel):
  "Heads-up — we have a planned infra migration (Sat 03/21 02:00-06:00 PT). You may see transient 5xx for a small percentage of requests. If you hit an error, please DM request-id + timestamp and we'll trace. Thanks for bearing with us."
- Email reply (customer-facing):
  "We are running a planned enhancement to improve request routing. During the maintenance window some requests may return transient errors. Please share any request ids and timestamps and our team will investigate. If you have an SLA, we will make sure to follow up directly."

Talking points for product leads/all-hands snippet (60s):
- Why: reduced cross-region latency + smoother routing, sets us up for feature X (weighted routing + A/B rollouts).
- What to expect: short maintenance window, some reconnects and rare 5xx; no data loss expected; we can roll back if error budgets spike.
- Ask of teams: avoid major launches same weekend; flag critical customers to CS.

Canary and observability plan (ops):
- Pre-smoke: synthetic traffic against a canary route for 30m.
- Canary metrics to watch: 5xx rate, p99 latency, connection drop counts, KV cache invalidation rate.
- Automated fallback: if 5xx > 2% for 5m, auto-route to legacy dataplane for traffic with tag "canary-legacy-allow".

Rollback play (concise):
- Trigger: sustained >5% 5xx or critical customer outage.
- Action: flip routing weight back to legacy control plane (action in playbook, requires SRE oncall + platform eng approval).
- Communication: update status page & notify CS and product channels.

Post-cutover checks (what I want as output):
- Latency/5xx dashboard 24h baseline vs post-change
- List of any customers who reported increased errors + tracing evidence
- Short blameless notes: what went as expected / surprises / next steps for automation

Unresolved questions I want to decide before locking comms:
- Do we include a proactive status page post at T+30m or only if errors observed? (leaning proactive: post a short "Migration complete, monitoring" update)
- Do we require CS to proactively reach out to customers with >1M monthly tokens? (leaning yes if they are in impacted regions)
- Final rollback threshold numbers (2% vs 5% for auto-fallback) — need SRE input.

Quick draft timeline for pushing to shared channel (my plan):
- Wed 03/11: Share this scratch with primary list for comments
- Fri 03/20 21:00 PT: Final pre-migration huddle (10-15m)
- Fri 03/20 22:00 PT: Pre-smoke run
- Sat 03/21 02:00 PT: Migration window start
- Sat 03/21 06:00 PT: Window end, initial validation
- Mon 03/23 09:00 PT: Post-check roundup in #platform-ops

Notes to self (personal):
- Keep comms short and utility-first; reduce jargon for CS copy.
- Capture one example trace that shows a reconnect flow for docs.
- Remind docs to include recommended retry headers sample.

Anything missing?
- Confirm rollback automation owner (I think Diego), confirm scripts and runbook location (Confluence link above).
- Confirm CS customer list for outreach (Priya to pull).

End of scratch. I'll tidy and push to #platform-ops when the rollback thresholds are confirmed.
